series_label: 河西走廊历史阅读 · 连载 26
title_en: Thirteen Horses Stayed: A Xuanquan Station Roster
title_zh: 十三匹马留置：悬泉置的一次传马调配
lead: 一份只有几行的传马记录，把驿路上“留下”和“出发”的两种责任摆在一起。

paragraphs.en: A surviving Xuanquan document counts forty-three relay horses. Thirteen were to remain at the station; thirty were assigned to ten relay carriages. This is a striking division of animals at a post near Dunhuang, on the western Hexi Corridor. The previous installment followed the fodder and labor needed to keep horses ready. This record takes the next step: readiness had to be turned into an allocation. Yet its few words leave a difficult question. If most of the horses were assigned to carriages, what work did the station still have to do for those that stayed?
paragraphs.zh: 一份现存的悬泉文书清点了四十三匹传马：十三匹留在置中，三十匹配给十乘传车。在河西走廊西段、敦煌附近的一处驿站，这样的分配值得细看。上一篇追踪的是让马匹保持可用所需的草料与劳作；这份记录则向前一步，显示“可用”还必须落实为一次调配。但寥寥几字也留下难题：多数马匹配给车辆之后，驿站对留下的马还要承担什么工作？

paragraphs.en: A relay station was part of an official travel system, not a place where any passerby could demand a horse. Officials and authorized travelers carried documents establishing their right to use its services. Xuanquan also handled messages and received people moving along the route. That meant its staff had to respond to journeys they could not reduce to one fixed daily pattern. Horses were costly working animals, while carts, drivers, fodder, and care all had to be available. A count of horses therefore mattered because it described a limited resource that people had to divide among competing duties.
paragraphs.zh: 驿置属于官方交通体系，并非路人都能随意索取马匹。官员及获准通行者需要凭文书使用相关服务。悬泉置还传递文书、接待沿路往来人员，工作人员面对的行程无法简化为每天固定不变的一套安排。马是需要成本的役畜，车辆、御者、草料和照料也都必须跟上。所以清点马匹并非单纯数数，而是在描述一种有限资源：人们必须把它分配到彼此争用的差事中。

paragraphs.en: The phrase about thirty horses and ten carriages shows an allocation of three horses per carriage in this entry. It does not establish that every Han relay carriage everywhere always used three horses. Nor does it tell us how far these particular carriages went, who rode in them, or whether all ten set out at once. A museum researcher interprets the entry as thirty horses serving the ten carriages while thirteen remained at Xuanquan. The distinction matters. A roster can show an administrative decision without preserving the full journeys that followed it.
paragraphs.zh: 这条记录中的三十匹马与十乘传车，算来每车分配三匹马；它并不能证明汉代各地每辆传车始终都用三匹马。我们也不知道这十乘车各走了多远、载了谁，或是否同时出发。甘肃简牍博物馆研究者将其解释为三十匹马供十乘传车使用，十三匹留在悬泉置。这个区别很重要：清册能够呈现一次行政决定，却未必保存决定之后每趟行程的全貌。

paragraphs.en: The thirteen remaining horses were not necessarily idle. Keeping animals at a station could preserve capacity for later official traffic and allow work and care to continue there. That is an interpretation of why a station might retain horses, not a stated purpose for these thirteen in the slip. The surviving line does not divide them into healthy animals, sick animals, reserves, or horses assigned to another task. It would be tempting to supply those categories from common sense. The safer reading is narrower: the document separates horses kept at Xuanquan from horses allocated to carriages, while leaving their subsequent use unrecorded.
paragraphs.zh: 留下的十三匹马未必无事可做。置中留马，可能是为了应对之后的公务交通，也便于继续安排使用与照料；但这是对驿站为何留马的一种解释，并不是简文写明的这十三匹马的用途。现存文字没有把它们分成健马、病马、备用马，或另有差事的马。凭常理替它补上这些类别很容易；较稳妥的读法却更窄：文书区分了留在悬泉置的马和配给车辆的马，之后如何使用则没有记录。

paragraphs.en: Other Xuanquan documents show how carefully a horse could be identified. A roster submitted by stable official Xin in the second year of Jianshi, 31 BCE, survives only in part. Its entries describe such features as color, sex, age, height, marks, and names. One horse was called Tiezhu. These identifying details helped officials distinguish an individual animal within a public inventory. They do not prove that Tiezhu belonged to the forty-three-horse count; the documents are separate. Put side by side, however, a name roster and an allocation entry show two distinct administrative needs: knowing which horse one had and deciding where working animals should go.
paragraphs.zh: 悬泉的其他文书表明，一匹马可以被辨认得多么细致。建始二年，即公元前31年，厩啬夫欣上报的一份传马名籍只部分留存。条目记有毛色、性别、年龄、身高、印记和名字等特征，其中一匹名叫“铁柱”。这些信息有助于官员在公有马匹清册中辨清个体，却不能证明“铁柱”属于那四十三匹马；两份文书彼此独立。把名籍与调配记录并读，能看见两项不同的行政需要：认清手上是哪匹马，以及决定役马分往何处。

paragraphs.en: For the people responsible for the station, those decisions carried practical consequences. A horse assigned to a carriage still needed a driver and feed; a horse kept behind still required care. Earlier records of fodder purchases, grass transport, illness, and official reprimands show that none of these supporting tasks could be assumed away. The forty-three-horse entry gives no date that securely connects it to those earlier examples. We cannot turn them into a single day's story. We can say that an allocation on paper depended on labor and supplies beyond the count itself, and that a shortage or sick horse could make a neat number harder to realize in practice.
paragraphs.zh: 对负责驿站的人而言，这些决定有实际后果。配给传车的马仍需御者和草料，留下的马也仍需照料。前文所见的饲料采购、运草、病马记录和官府申饬说明，这些配套工作不能凭空省略。四十三匹马的记录没有一个能与那些例子确切相连的日期，不能把它们拼成同一天的故事。但可以说，纸上的调配依赖数字之外的劳力与物资；一旦缺马或有马患病，整齐的数字在实际执行时就更难兑现。

paragraphs.en: There is also a difference between allocating a carriage and completing a journey. The surviving count does not include a departure log, a destination list, or a receipt from the next station. It cannot tell us how many official travelers were carried, whether the carriages returned, or how quickly the horses recovered. Even the word 'remained' is a snapshot, not a permanent status. The record's value lies in showing that Xuanquan staff had to balance immediate service against capacity at home. Its silence reminds us how much of a road's history disappears when only one kind of account survives.
paragraphs.zh: 把车马分配出去，与走完一趟路也有区别。这份现存清点没有附上出发簿、目的地清单，或下一站的收讫记录。它不能告诉我们载了多少公务旅客、传车是否返回，或马匹多快恢复体力。即使“留置”二字，说明的也是某一时点的状态，并非永远不变的身份。记录的价值在于让人看见，悬泉置人员必须在眼前的服务需求与站内保有的能力之间权衡；它的沉默也提醒我们，若只存一种账目，道路史会失去多少细节。

paragraphs.en: The opening question can now be answered within the evidence. Thirteen horses remained under the station's responsibility while thirty were assigned to ten carriages; both groups still depended on people, feed, and continued management. We do not know the later duties of the thirteen or the routes taken by the thirty. The entry captures a choice rather than a completed journey. After following the costs of keeping horses ready, we can see how readiness was divided on a working day at Xuanquan. The next trace to seek is a dated movement record that links an assigned carriage or named horse to a particular trip.
paragraphs.zh: 开篇的问题，可以在证据允许的范围内回答：十三匹马仍由驿站负责，三十匹配给十乘传车；两组马都离不开人、草料和持续管理。那十三匹马后来做了什么、三十匹马走了哪些路，我们并不知道。这条简文捕捉的是一次选择，而不是一趟已经完成的行程。追过养马待命的成本之后，我们又看见悬泉置如何把这份能力分配出去。下一条值得寻找的线索，是有日期的出入记录，能将某乘传车或某匹有名可查的马与一次具体行程相连。

questions.q: How were the forty-three horses divided in the surviving entry?
questions.a: Thirteen remained at Xuanquan, while thirty were assigned to ten relay carriages.

questions.q: Why can't Tiezhu be identified as one of those forty-three horses?
questions.a: Tiezhu appears in a separate, partly preserved name roster; no surviving link joins the two documents.

questions.q: What does the entry fail to show about the carriages?
questions.a: It does not show their destinations, passengers, departures, returns, or completed journeys.
